notes:
Five bullets of the seven are steps, and the shape is simple once the OR is seen for what it is. Bullet 2 states the quest's central choice -- kill the mobs for the drop, or click three ???s in the zone for key items that combine into the same item -- and its sub-bullets are Sneak/Invisible advice. Bullet 3 is Trust strategy and is not a step; neither is the 'Maps are located below' line, the map table, nor the 'Note:' paragraph. That Note is nonetheless the best confirmation on the page that the ITEM is the right observable: once you hold one of the three, the ???s in that zone go quiet regardless of how many fragments you have. So each collection step carries its item as evidence and the OR vanishes into it -- both routes end with the same thing in your inventory, and nothing needs an items_alt.

The fragment key items cannot serve instead even if I wanted them to: 'Bomb coal fragment', 'Exoray mold crumb' and 'Ancient papyrus shred' are all non-unique names in res/key_items.lua and the resolver rejects them rather than guess an id. They are also counted three-at-a-time, which no key item can express.

'The required items may be obtained in any order' is explicit, so the three collection steps share a group and all draw at once. Each zone is ONE step and not three examines: the three ???s in a zone are unmarkable and individually unobservable, which is exactly the case the guide merges -- so their grids sit in the note instead of the grid field. Everything else under bullets 4-6 is routing (the Pouch of weighted stones for the first Banishing Gate, the East Plate versus the Magicked astrolabe in the Necropolis, the Survival Manual detour, which graves drop you through the floor) and stays in notes.

Bullet 5 writes the zone 'Crawler's Nest' and the map table writes 'Crawlers' Nest'; both resolve to 197 and the game's spelling is used. The monsters are written only in the plural in bullets 4-6, but 'Explosure' and 'Exoray' also appear in the singular in bullet 3; 'Lich' is the plain singular of the page's 'Liches'. Level 50 on any job is the level gate restated, so jobs stays empty. The reward is a level cap raise, not an item, so the final trade has no evidence and none was reached for.

Undead here aggro low HP through Sneak and Invisible, and Invisible must be dropped to click a ???.

three ???s: on the path from (I-10) on Map 1 heading for Map 3, at (I-6) on Map 3 further along that path, and at (G-10) on Map 2 among the Exorays -- or kill Exorays for the drop instead. Both routes run out of the 'sack room'; the third takes the northwest tunnel, not the dead end with scorpions. Sneak keeps the Exorays off you.

three ???s at (F-7), (F-9) and (H-9) on Map 1, each in the corner of a room of Liches around a Brazier; zone in from Batallia Downs (I/J-10). Or kill Liches for the drop instead -- the page writes them only as 'Liches'. If the left path is walled off, take the East Plate behind the Gravestone to open it, or carry a Magicked astrolabe (10,000 gil from Churano-Shurano, Windurst Waters (F-8)) and open the gates yourself. Do not walk over the square graves; some drop you to a lower level.
all three items; the reward is the level cap raised to 55, which is nothing you can hold, so this step has no evidence

notes:
Twenty-six bullets, but the middle three quarters of them are one choice made three times. Bullet 3 hands you ONE of three Iridal cores and the '== Iridal core of the ... ==' headings are branches, not stages: bullets 4-8 are the level 109 fight, 9-14 the 125, 15-22 the 135. Read as a sequence this page would produce a fifteen-rung ladder that nobody can ever complete.

The three branch entries are modelled as three grouped 'examine Hazy Rune' steps, one per zone, each carrying its own core in items. A step has one zone, so they cannot be merged; and all three have to be drawable while the player is still deciding, which is what the group gives. That is the group mechanism used for an OR rather than for a set, which is a deliberate stretch and is flagged -- but nothing depends on 'all done', because none of the three carries evidence.

The fight is then ONE step with no zone, the Waking the Beast shape: the same Arcus Blades in whichever battlefield you entered, so no zone is honest and the target is none. It carries the Arcus fiber. Here is the one real weakness: the page states the Refined Ra'Kaznar fiber transforming into an Arcus fiber ONLY in bullet 7, the 109 branch -- bullets 13 and 20 list Bayld, synthesis materials and a Codex and say nothing about the fiber. Arcus fiber is in the header's own Item Reqs and the Afterwards section is shared by all three branches, so I read it as universal. That inference is why this quest is medium and not high; if it is wrong, the two harder branches simply lose an anchor and fall back on the session latch.

Not steps: bullets 6, 12 and 19 are the monster's spell list, 7, 13 and 20 are rewards, 21 is a title, and 8, 14 and 22 are 'proceed to the Afterwards section below' -- navigation inside the page. Bullet 1's sub-bullets are eligibility notes (one relic piece is enough, a Kupon A-AF +3 flag does not work, this is not the Rune Fencer quest NPC). Bullet 26 is the repeat, once per conquest tally, which nothing observable reports.

The '== Afterwards ==' bullets 23-26 are still inside the Walkthrough and keep their numbering, so no restart applies to them; bullet 23 is the page's own 'Optional:'. The separate '## After the walkthrough: The Rest of the Armor' section, whose bullets do restart at [1], is post-quest armour forging -- it begins after the Surcoat is already in hand, is gated one piece per game day, and is a different transaction from this quest -- so none of it is a step here.

'Adoulin' is not one of the nine fame regions and resolves to nothing, so region is null and only the raw string is kept. 'Level: 99 Rune Fencer' is both gates.

ADVERSARIAL PASS (stage D): the reading survives on evidence, ordering, zones, targets and gates -- every name is in the page text and resolves, no item is evidence twice, no reward was used as evidence (Arcus fiber is an Item Req, not a Reward; the Erilaz Surcoat and the title are Rewards and carry none), and bullets 23-26 really do continue the Walkthrough's numbering. The one thing that did not survive is the confidence on steps 4-6. They are an XOR the schema has no way to say: 'group' means an unordered set in which every member is done, and these three are alternatives of which exactly one is done. Marking them optional would be worse -- it would suppress the marker for the one place the player actually has to go -- so the shape is kept and the three steps are demoted to medium instead. The Arcus fiber inference on step 7 was re-checked and left standing: the page is silent for the 125 and 135 branches rather than contradictory, the Afterwards section is shared by all three, and nulling it would cost the 109 branch its only anchor to buy nothing.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 7: The Refined Ra'Kaznar fiber becoming an Arcus fiber is stated by the page only for the 109 branch; it is read as universal here, which is the quest's medium confidence.
